It sounds frustrating to deal with focus and procrastination challenges, especially when they're affecting your work. Many people have experienced increased concentration difficulties since the pandemic, whether due to ADHD, stress, burnout, changes in routine, or other factors. If you suspect ADHD, consider speaking with a healthcare professional or mental health provider who can properly evaluate your symptoms and discuss treatment options, which might include therapy, medication, or both.

In the meantime, some strategies that can help include breaking tasks into very small steps, using timers for short focused work periods, removing distractions from your environment, and being compassionate with yourself when things feel difficult. Starting with just five minutes on a task can sometimes help overcome the initial resistance. You might also find it helpful to identify whether anxiety, perfectionism, or exhaustion are contributing to the procrastination. You don't have to figure this out alone—reaching out for professional support is a valid and practical step.
